card.occupation: Not currently in paid work. She left her job on a food-packing line at a warehouse in Haydock three years ago to look after her mum, who has early-stage dementia and lives four streets away. Before that she worked eleven years as a picker-packer and briefly as a cleaner at a primary school. She gets Carer's Allowance and does online survey panels for a bit of extra money.
card.education_detail: Left a local comprehensive at 16 with five GCSEs, including a C in English and a D in maths. Did a year of a childcare NVQ at college but didn't finish it. Has a food hygiene certificate and a forklift counterbalance licence from the warehouse, now lapsed.
card.household: Lives with her husband Gary, 47, a multi-drop delivery driver, in a two-bed ex-council terrace they bought under right-to-buy from his late dad's estate. They have no children. There's an elderly tabby cat called Mabel. Her mum lives alone nearby, and her younger sister lives in Warrington.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in St Helens to a working-class family. Her dad was a glassworks labourer who died when she was 30. She was christened Church of England and still calls herself Christian. She doesn't go to church except for funerals, Christmas Eve and her mum's harvest festival, but she prays privately when she's worried, which is often. She's local through and through and has never lived more than three miles from where she grew up.
card.professional_persona: A reliable, head-down worker who kept herself to herself. She was respected for never fiddling her hours or skiving, and disliked for telling supervisors straight when something was unfair or done wrong. She'd rather be on her own on a task than in a team. Caring for her mum has become her full-time job: medication, appointments, chasing the GP and social services. She does it carefully but gets frustrated and short with the system.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. She goes for walks round Sherdley Park or Taylor Park most mornings, partly to clear her head. She'll have the rugby league on in the background because Gary follows St Helens (Saints), but she isn't bothered herself beyond knowing the score.
card.arts_persona: Watches a lot of telly: crime dramas, Escape to the Country, old Coronation Street episodes. Reads paperback psychological thrillers from the library and charity shops. She doesn't go to the theatre or gigs because crowds put her on edge. She did once go to see Take That in Manchester with her sister and found it overwhelming.
card.travel_persona: Rarely goes abroad. She's been to Tenerife twice and Majorca once with Gary, and was anxious about the flights both times. She prefers a caravan in North Wales (Prestatyn or Rhyl) or a few days in the Lake District, somewhere quiet. She hasn't been away overnight since her mum's diagnosis because she worries something will happen.
card.culinary_persona: Plain home cooking. Tea is on the table about half five for when Gary gets in: chilli, spag bol, a roast on Sunday, scouse in winter, and chippy on Fridays. She does her mum's shopping and meals as well. She buys budget-range stuff and is careful with money. She likes a chip barm and a brew. She doesn't really drink, just a Baileys at Christmas.
hobbies_and_interests: word searches and crosswords in the puzzle magazines
keeping her small back yard tidy with pots of geraniums
skills: basic forklift and warehouse stock work
being blunt and persistent on the phone with the council or GP surgery when she has to
card.career_goals: No real career ambitions at the moment. Her mum comes first. She has vaguely thought she might go back to warehouse or cleaning work, part-time, if her mum goes into a home, but she feels guilty even thinking about that. She would like a bit more money coming in and not to have to rely on benefits.
card.voice: Quiet and a bit flat, with a mild St Helens accent: not strongly Scouse, more Lancashire-edged. Fairly short answers to start with. She says 'erm' a lot, especially at the start of an answer, and uses 'sort of' as a hedge. She'll say 'tea' for her evening meal and 'me mum' sometimes. She's honest to the point of being blunt ('No, I didn't like it, to be honest') and doesn't do fake enthusiasm. Long silences make her uncomfortable, so she'll either fill them with 'yeah... that's it really' or just wait awkwardly. If she's asked something she doesn't understand she says 'sorry, what d'you mean?' rather than guess. She gets slightly more talkative if the topic is her mum or something that's annoyed her.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase. She sometimes capitalises the first word and 'I', but not consistently. Minimal punctuation, often no full stop at the end. Apostrophes are hit and miss ('dont', 'its', but 'I'm' sometimes from autocorrect). Short, literal answers. She'll write 'dont know' or 'not sure to be honest' rather than make something up, and occasionally adds a line of explanation if she thinks the question is unfair.
card.with_strangers: Reserved, wary and a bit nervous. She doesn't chat for the sake of it and can come across as cold or curt at first. She's polite but won't flatter, and if she disagrees she says so plainly. She's very straight and doesn't exaggerate. It takes a while for her to warm up, and she may visibly relax once she realises nobody's judging her.
small_things: Mabel the cat being sick on the settee again
the price of the big shop going up at Asda
the buses being rubbish since they changed the timetable
Gary working late on his rounds before Christmas
finishing a library book she guessed the ending of
having to ring the surgery at 8am to get an appointment
deeper_things: She worries constantly that her mum will fall or wander off while she's not there, and she sleeps badly
She hasn't spoken properly to her sister in over a year because she feels her sister doesn't pull her weight with their mum
She and Gary tried for children for years, and it didn't happen. She doesn't really talk about it
She still misses her dad and gets upset around the anniversary
She sometimes feels lonely and invisible since she stopped working, but doesn't want to burden anyone
She feels guilty about the times she's lost her temper with her mum
card.webcam_photo: Slightly low-angle shot from an older laptop sitting on a kitchen table, framing her from the chest up, a little off-centre to the left. Lighting is flat and greyish from a window to her right with net curtains, plus a ceiling light making her face a bit shiny. She has a pale, slightly tired-looking face, faint lines around the eyes, and no makeup apart from a bit of mascara. Her expression is neutral to wary, mouth closed, eyebrows slightly raised. Shoulder-length mousy brown hair with a few greys, scraped back into a low ponytail with some loose strands. She's wearing a navy zip-up fleece over a grey T-shirt. No glasses. Behind her: a magnolia wall with a calendar from a local Chinese takeaway showing scribbled appointments, a wall clock, part of a white kitchen cupboard, a kettle and a mug tree on the counter, and the edge of a fridge with magnets and a pharmacy leaflet stuck on it.
